supporting_observations.claim: Repeated failures for svc-render occurred at roughly one-minute intervals from FILE-NWD-01, beginning at 13:32:41 and continuing through at least 13:47:47. The FILE-NWD-01 events report logon type 3 and bad-password substatus 0xc000006a.
Domain-controller records also show failed authentication for svc-render from FILE-NWD-01, including NTLM validation failures and Kerberos pre-authentication failures.

The failure pattern is consistent with the supplied context that svc-render runs and re-authenticates every minute and that its password was scheduled for rotation at 13:30 UTC, after which the job needed a manual update. This supports a plausible benign explanation, but does not verify that the rotation occurred or the job was updated incorrectly.

At 13:36:09, WS-NBLAKE-01 recorded a PowerShell process running as SYSTEM using explicit credentials for svc-render while targeting PROXY-NWD-01. This is outside the expected FILE-NWD-01 service-job pattern in the supplied context and warrants investigation; the event alone does not show whether authentication or proxy access succeeded.

known_telemetry_limitations: The supplied records do not establish whether the scheduled password rotation occurred, when it took effect, or whether the RenderQueue job was updated.
The explicit-credentials event provides a process path but no command line, script contents, process ancestry, or user/operator attribution.
No proxy access or authentication result is provided for the svc-render credential use from WS-NBLAKE-01.
The supplied records show failures but do not provide a complete view of successful authentications or other activity by svc-render during the review window.
claims_not_established: That the svc-render failures were caused by the scheduled password rotation rather than another cause.
That the svc-render credentials were successfully used from WS-NBLAKE-01 or that the proxy request succeeded.
That the PowerShell activity on WS-NBLAKE-01 was authorized, malicious, or related to the failed RenderQueue logons.
That an attacker obtained or attempted to compromise svc-render.
additional_evidence_needed: Password-change and account-management audit records for svc-render around 13:30 UTC, plus RenderQueue configuration or job-update history.
Process creation, PowerShell logging, script contents, and process ancestry for the 13:36 activity on WS-NBLAKE-01.
PROXY-NWD-01 authentication and access logs around 13:36 UTC to determine whether the explicit credential use produced a request or successful authentication.
Authentication records for svc-render across the full review window, including any successful logons.
